perPaper.paper_title: The Lunar Navigation Signal Is Unauthenticated: Sizing the Spoofing and Jamming Attack Surface of the LunaNet Augmented Forward Signal
perPaper.core_thesis: The LunaNet Augmented Forward Signal (AFS) that NASA/ESA/JAXA will broadcast carries no signal-level authentication. A closed-form link budget shows the AFS reaches the lunar surface at ~-140.6 dBW, ~15.6 dB (factor ~36, 12-18 dB band) below terrestrial GPS at -125 dBW, so jamming/spoofing margins are proportionally thinner. Under a 3 dB capture / 30 dB denial J/S criterion a surface spoofer needs only 0.022 mW at 1 km and 0.222 W at 100 km; a surface attacker is bounded by the airless horizon (2 m mast -> 5 km, 1000 m ridge -> 61 km) but a single ~40 W orbital transmitter illuminates the whole visible hemisphere, and no lunar monitoring network exists. The paper sizes a three-layer defense (OSNMA-style message authentication, cross-sensor IMU/TRN integrity, sparse known-location monitors), argues the fix requires no new physics, and marks every result Validated (closed-form radiometry) or Modelled (representative service geometry).

analyses.name: Received AFS surface power link budget (-140.6 dBW)
analyses.computes: Free-space path loss L_fs=(4*pi*R*f/c)^2 and P_rx = P_sat*G_sat*G_user/L_fs at the Table-1 operating point (f=2.4 GHz, EIRP 20 W+13 dBi, 3000 km slant, G_user 3 dBi), giving ~-140.6 dBW (-110.6 dBm).

analyses.name: Lunar power deficit vs terrestrial GPS (15.6 dB / factor ~36)
analyses.computes: Difference of modelled lunar P_rx and an imported GPS L1 C/A reference (-125 dBW): -125-(-140.6)=15.6 dB, a linear factor ~36.

analyses.name: Attacker required transmit power vs standoff (spoof/jam curves)
analyses.computes: Inverts the free-space attacker link P_atk=P_tx*G_tx*G_user/(4*pi*d*f/c)^2 set to the required J/S to solve P_tx(d): spoof (3 dB) 0.022 mW@1km, 8.9 mW@20km, 0.222 W@100km; jam (30 dB) ~1000x more. Plotted as Fig 1a.

analyses.name: Capture (3 dB) vs denial (30 dB) J/S thresholds
analyses.computes: Static order-of-magnitude J/S ratios used as the capture and denial criteria that scale the entire attacker-power table.

analyses.name: Horizon-limited surface reach
analyses.computes: Geometric horizon of a mast height h on airless sphere R_moon: d_hor=sqrt(2*R_moon*h+h^2). 2 m->5 km, 10 m->8 km, 100 m->21 km, 1000 m->61 km.

analyses.name: Whole-hemisphere orbital transmitter footprint
analyses.computes: A single ~40 W, 13 dBi orbital transmitter at the Table-1 slant range meets the 3 dB spoof-capture criterion across the entire visible hemisphere, under a single uniform-beam assumption (no antenna-pattern rolloff, no edge-of-disk grazing).

analyses.name: Power-deficit sensitivity band
analyses.computes: Sweep of GPS reference (-125 to -128.5 dBW), satellite EIRP, and slant range showing the deficit stays in a 12-18 dB band (factor 16-63); reconciles the rounded 32x figure vs unrounded 36x text.

analyses.name: Six-attribute lunar-vs-terrestrial security comparison (Fig 1b)
analyses.computes: Consolidates received-power deficit, specified authentication, receiver cross-checks, spoof power at 1 km, monitoring network, and physical access into a comparison across lunar AFS vs terrestrial GNSS.

analyses.name: Defense Layer 1: OSNMA-style NMA fits the AFS budget
analyses.computes: Assertion that a TESLA delayed-disclosure navigation-message-authentication layer has overhead (data-rate fraction + bounded latency) fitting within the AFS message/timing budget.

analyses.name: Defense Layer 2: cross-sensor IMU/TRN integrity
analyses.computes: Assertion that an inertial + terrain-relative-navigation cross-check (RAIM-analogous, independent sensing modality) catches the residual capture surviving authentication.

analyses.name: Defense Layer 3: sparse known-location monitors
analyses.computes: Assertion that a few surveyed known-location monitor receivers with a strong prior on expected power/timing/geometry raise the difficulty of an undetected wide-area (orbital) attack.

verified_gaps.title: Tracking-loop pull-in spoof-capture model (replace static 3 dB J/S)
verified_gaps.description: The paper's headline capture criterion is a static J/S=3 dB threshold, flagged in Sec 6 as a calibration input for an unhardened receiver. Model capture instead as code/carrier tracking-loop pull-in: whether the spoofer captures the DLL/PLL as a function of power advantage (J/S), code/carrier-phase alignment/offset, loop bandwidth, and lock time. The primitives exist (sdr::track DLL+PLL, synth_if, correlate; spoof_detect power_advantage_db/carrier_aligned knobs) but there is no analysis that drives an authentic+spoofer composite IF through the loop and reports capture-vs-lock-time / capture-J/S. Build a spoof-capture analysis composing sdr::track over a two-signal IF and emit a capture map (J/S x carrier offset x lock time).
verified_gaps.paper_need: Upgrade the capture criterion from an asserted 3 dB threshold to a computed pull-in result, converting Sec 3/Fig 1a from a threshold-scaled table into a receiver-dynamics analysis.
verified_gaps.suggested_location: new src/spoof_capture.rs composing sdr::{synth_if,track,correlate}; expose a 'spoof-capture' scenario in api.rs; regression under tests/
verified_gaps.validation_oracle: TEXBAT/OAKBAT raw-IF spoofing records via realdata/iqif + tests/spoof_texbat_validation.rs (capture outcome vs measured lock), and the closed-form DLL/PLL pull-in range from Kaplan & Hegarty ch.8/ch.14 as an analytic cross-check.
verified_gaps.verify_evidence: Confirmed primitives present but no capture analysis. src/sdr.rs has synth_if (l264, single-signal IF: one code/carrier/amp), correlate (l237), track (l463, takes a single &[Cf64] IQ block). src/spoof_detect.rs exposes power_advantage_db (l76) and carrier_aligned (l79) but run_spoof_detect (l189) computes measured_dbm = floor + power_advantage_db (l222) and applies static AGC/SQM/RAIM thresholds — it never runs a two-signal composite IF through a tracking loop to compute pull-in vs lock time. No src/spoof_capture.rs (ls src grep capture empty). synth_if generates only one signal so there is no authentic+spoofer superposition path today. Genuine upgrade gap.

perPaper.paper_title: The Cost of Lunar South-Polar Geometry, and Surface Beacons as the Efficient Fix: A Dilution-of-Precision Analysis
perPaper.core_thesis: Orbit-only ELFO lunar constellations pay a steep satellite-count cost for south-polar geometry because visible satellites cluster into a small overhead solid angle: median GDOP stays ~16-21 at the planned 4-6 satellites and only crosses 6 near N~12. Three surface ranging beacons (lunar pseudolites) on 2 km elevated terrain ringing a -80 deg user supply the missing near-horizon horizontal diversity, cutting median GDOP from 16.2 to 1.6 (factor ~10, better than a 24-satellite fleet) at a fraction of the cost. The airless-body geometric horizon makes beacon siting a genuine placement optimization. The GDOP engine is Validated; the constellation and beacon scenario are Modelled.

analyses.name: ELFO constellation model + Kepler phasing propagation
analyses.computes: A representative elliptical lunar frozen orbit (sma 6142 km, e=0.6, i=57.7 deg, argp=90 deg for apolune over the south pole), with satellites propagated by Kepler phasing across planes/mean anomaly in MCI, rotated to MCMF.

analyses.name: Visibility test: 5-deg elevation mask + lunar-limb occultation
analyses.computes: A satellite is visible iff elevation >= 5 deg mask and its line of sight is not occulted by the lunar limb (R=1737.4 km). For a surface user, elevation>=0 already excludes below-limb satellites.

analyses.name: Geometry matrix H and scalar GDOP
analyses.computes: Forms H from unit LOS vectors augmented with a clock column; GDOP = sqrt(tr[(H^T H)^-1]).

analyses.name: Time-averaged availability + median GDOP at the pole
analyses.computes: Time-average over one orbital cycle: availability = fraction of time with >=4 visible satellites; median GDOP over the samples. GDOP tagged Validated, constellation tagged Modelled.

analyses.name: Satellite-count sweep (N=4..24)
analyses.computes: Table 1: for N in {4,5,6,8,10,12,16,24} reports availability, median GDOP, and fraction of time below GDOP 6; shows median crosses 6 near N~12, non-monotonic bump at N=6.

analyses.name: Spatial GDOP + availability map
analyses.computes: GDOP and availability evaluated on a grid over -70 to -90 deg latitude and all longitudes, time-averaged, for a six-satellite constellation.

analyses.name: Surface-beacon (pseudolite) augmentation of H
analyses.computes: Adds surface ranging beacons as extra ranging rows (near-horizon LOS with large horizontal components) to the geometry matrix H, conditioning the near-vertical satellite geometry.

analyses.name: Surface-to-surface horizon-bounded visibility (airless body)
analyses.computes: With no atmospheric refraction, surface-to-surface LOS is bounded by the geometric horizon set by beacon/user heights; a beacon at 50 km on 2 km terrain gives ~1.5 deg elevation while a flat-terrain beacon at 180 km falls below the horizon and contributes nothing.

analyses.name: Beacon before/after GDOP table for -80 deg user
analyses.computes: Table 2: 6-sat ELFO only -> median GDOP 16.2, 15% time below 6; 6-sat ELFO + 3 beacons -> median GDOP 1.6, 100% below 6 (factor ~10, better than a 24-sat fleet at 3.4).

analyses.name: Beacon horizon range vs height (closed form)
analyses.computes: Geometric horizon distance as a function of beacon and user height on a sphere of radius R (airless), used to justify 50 km ring on 2 km terrain vs 180 km flat.

analyses.name: Figure 1 three-panel composite

perPaper.paper_title: Realizing Coordinated Lunar Time at a User Is Frame-Limited, Not Clock-Limited: A Systems Error Budget
perPaper.core_thesis: Given a defined Coordinated Lunar Time (TCL/TL), the binding constraint on a user realizing it to the ~1 ns level positioning needs is NOT the atomic clock. Placing clock stability, Earth-Moon time-transfer link floors, and lunar frame/ephemeris knowledge on one axis (timing error at tau=1 day, quadrature-summed), the terms that meet 1 ns are a ground optical master clock (0.009 ns), optical two-way transfer (0.035 ns), post-processed frame (0.90 ns) and a space PHM (0.99 ns); the terms that MISS are real-time frame/ephemeris knowledge (~50 ns, the ~15 m real-time position budget as light time) and a SWaP-limited 500 g miniRAFS (~151 ns/day). Roadmap implication: the highest-leverage investment is real-time frame/ephemeris prediction (an estimation problem), not further clock improvement.

verified_gaps.title: Independently DERIVE the real-time lunar frame/ephemeris position-error growth (the ~15 m -> ~50 ns term) instead of importing it
verified_gaps.description: The headline bottleneck (real-time frame/ephemeris ~50 ns) is currently IMPORTED as a 15 m position budget and converted by light time. The upgrade prescription is to derive it: propagate a lunar OD + frame-realisation estimate forward through prediction latency and show the predicted (real-time) position error grows to ~15 m while the post-processed (smoothed/fitted) error settles to ~0.27 m. perPaper.paper_title: The lunar real-time frame gap is an Earth-orientation prediction problem: decomposing the 15 m to sub-meter budget
perPaper.core_thesis: The lumped lunar real-time frame budget (~15 m real-time vs ~0.27 m post-processed, worth ~50 ns) is largely Earth-orientation (UT1-UTC) prediction error amplified by the Earth-Moon lever arm (delta_r = D_EM * omega_earth * delta_UT1). Inverting the exact lever arm on the two published lunar budgets recovers IERS final (~0.010 ms) and multi-day-predicted (~0.5 ms, ~5-day) UT1 accuracies, so the real-time gap is an EOP-prediction gap. The prescribed lever is hardware-free: shortening the EOP prediction horizon from ~5 days to ~1 day buys ~5x in real-time lunar position knowledge from the ground segment. The lever arm is Validated (exact geometry); the error-growth-vs-horizon curve is a two-anchor power law (Modelled) explicitly flagged for replacement by real IERS Bulletin-A prediction statistics.

perPaper.paper_title: Precision Without Continuity: Why Lunar Optical PNT Needs an RF Integrity Backstop, and a Hybrid Handoff Framework
perPaper.core_thesis: Optical Earth-Moon links are 100-1000x more precise than RF (mm/ps vs m/ns) but weather- and pointing-limited: a single optical ground station is available ~53% of the time and even a 5-6 station diversity network saturates near 95-96%, short of RF's >99.5%. Because a PNT service demands continuity and integrity, not just precision, an optical-only architecture is not a service. The resolution and open problem is a hybrid: RF provides always-on continuity plus an independent cross-modality integrity channel while optical provides precision, bound by a discontinuity-free receiver handoff and a joint availability/precision/integrity trade specification. The paper is explicit that the link/availability numbers are Modelled and that the hybrid integrity framing is the (incremental) contribution.

perPaper.paper_title: Cislunar Positioning Is an Observability Problem, Not a Geometry Problem: Why Snapshot GDOP Does Not Apply to DRO and Libration Constellations
perPaper.core_thesis: Snapshot GDOP is structurally inapplicable to cislunar full-state orbit determination: for a CR3BP DRO constellation the instantaneous inter-satellite ranging Jacobian is rank-deficient (rank 1 of 4, velocity unobservable) so GDOP is undefined, and full-state observability accrues only over a ~1 hour tracking arc as CR3BP dynamics propagate position information into velocity through the state-transition matrix; the correct figure of merit is a functional of the observability Gramian (rank, minimum eigenvalue, condition number) along the orbit rather than snapshot GDOP.

perPaper.paper_title: Defense-in-depth for lunar PNT: per-vector degradation of a layered position-navigation-timing architecture under a conflict baseline
perPaper.core_thesis: Lunar PNT should be specified against a conflict baseline: a four-layer defense-in-depth architecture (Earth-GNSS, lunar orbital, surface beacons, onboard INS+optical TRN), fused by inverse-variance weighting, degrades gracefully and keeps total-loss probability near 10% at full single-domain contest versus ~72% for the two-layer default (a ~7x reduction). Reported per attack vector rather than as a composite score, the un-jammable self-contained INS/TRN layer is the decisive catastrophic-risk reducer and broadband jamming is the sharpest adversary vector.

analyses.name: Four-layer PNT layer model (availability, standalone 1σ accuracy, per-vector vulnerability profile)
analyses.computes: Table 1: Earth-GNSS (0.60/50 m/spoof+jam), Lunar orbital LANS/ELFO (0.99/15 m/spoof+jam+kinetic), Surface beacons (1.00/3 m/jam), Onboard INS+optical TRN (1.00/25 m/cyber only). Parametric layer descriptors feeding fusion and threat sim.

analyses.name: Inverse-variance fusion of heterogeneous layers
analyses.computes: Fused 1σ = (Σ_i 1/a_i²)^(-1/2), the standard independent-measurement result; combines the standalone accuracies of surviving layers into a single fused position error.

analyses.name: Multi-vector Monte-Carlo threat simulation
analyses.computes: 20000 trials/point; each layer denied with probability vulnerability_i × intensity × vector-weight; threat intensity swept 0→2; usable PNT defined as fused error <10 m; total loss = no layer surviving. Seeded/reproducible.

analyses.name: Total-loss probability vs threat intensity (4/3/2-layer)

analyses.name: Median fused position error vs threat intensity
analyses.computes: Fig 1a: median fused position error as a function of intensity; four-layer holds sub-10 m through moderate contest then falls back to ~25 m onboard-only floor (graceful degradation).

analyses.name: Per-vector graceful-degradation / usable-PNT survival curves

synthesis.summary: Master build ledger synthesizing 55 verified gaps across 7 lunar/cislunar PNT preprints (P1 signal-security, P2 surface-beacon DOP, P3 coordinated-lunar-time budget, P4 real-time-frame/EOP, P5 optical/RF hybrid, P6 cislunar observability, P7 conflict resilience) against Kshana (public engine) + kshana-pro (overlay). Deduped: the airless-body geometric-horizon helper is built ONCE (L01) serving P1+P2 instead of twice; the lunar frame/ephemeris prediction covariance is built ONCE (L13) serving P3+P4, with P4's placeholder-covariance gap (L21) depending on it rather than rebuilding. 17 items are is_upgrade_prescription=true (all P0): they convert imported/asserted headline numbers into Kshana-derived results — e.g. spoof capture from static 3 dB J/S to tracking-loop pull-in (L03), the ~50 ns real-time frame term from imported 15 m budget to OD-covariance-derived prediction error (L13) and to a data-derived IERS UT1 prediction curve × Earth-Moon lever arm (L18/L19), the cislunar observability Gramian (L27), and the correlated/sourced conflict threat model (L35). 33 items land in public kshana (core scientific analysis, scenarios, oracles, fixtures); 22 in kshana-pro (paper-grade packs, branded reports, committed CSVs, figure renderers). Ordered into 10 independently shippable, single-repo phases: five kshana core phases (one per paper cluster) each followed by its kshana-pro deliverable phase, so every phase is a clean commit and pack phases only run after their core analyses land. Dependencies wired so no pack precedes its core analysis and no scenario/report precedes the function it renders.

themes.description: Free-space path loss, received power/CN0, J/S vs standoff, spoof/jam capture, and per-vector jamming/spoofing realism. Kshana linkbudget.rs/jamming.rs/spoof_detect.rs already supply the closed-form primitives; gaps are inverse solvers, tracking-loop capture, antenna-pattern footprints, NMA sizing, and monitor-network detection.

Geometric horizon on an atmosphereless Moon, surface-to-surface visibility, DOP/GDOP over selenographic grids, and beacon augmentation of H. The validated orbit::dop kernel and selenographic_to_mcmf exist; gaps are the horizon helper, beacon-augmented DOP, median-GDOP aggregates/maps, and (for cislunar) why snapshot GDOP is structurally inapplicable.

Three-term ADEV synthesis, accumulated clock error, seven-term quadrature budget with tau sweep, named-clock catalogue, and deterministic relativistic scale terms. powerlaw.rs/holdover.rs/lunar_time.rs supply forward models; gaps are the tau-swept budget assembler, clock-spec library, topographic/TCG-TCL terms, and a forward-ADEV external oracle.

The dominant real-time lunar frame error decomposed as OD+frame prediction covariance (P3) and as IERS UT1 prediction error amplified by the Earth-Moon lever arm (P4). eop.rs/cio.rs/lunar_frame_realise.rs/lunar_od.rs exist; gaps are prediction-latency covariance propagation, a Bulletin-A predicted-column parser + prediction-error-vs-horizon curve, and the lever-arm mapping.

Independent-channel integrity: cross-sensor IMU/TRN spoof-walk bounds, cross-modality RF+optical RAIM protection levels, discontinuity-free filter handoff, joint availability/precision/integrity FoM, and layered defense-in-depth Monte-Carlo. raim.rs/tpl.rs/fusion/*/resilience/* supply primitives; gaps are the heterogeneous-modality and layered-conflict compositions.

Full-state observability over a tracking arc via the observability Gramian (rank, min eigenvalue, condition), CR3BP STM propagation, inter-satellite range/range-rate Jacobians, and SRIF/batch validation. cr3bp.rs (variational STM), fim.rs (eig/rank/condition), deepspace_od.rs (SRIF) exist; the arc-sweep Gramian assembly and DRO seeder are the gaps.
